taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-30, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 74.2 | 15.31 | 15.31
2 | 27.3 | 18.79 | 34.10
3 | 76.3 | 5.06 | 39.16
4 | 96.3 | 4.07 | 43.23
5 | 138.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as K-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-30, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-30 in survey area T features a five-layer resistivity profile. The measured resistivities for the layers are 74.2, 27.3, 76.3, 96.3, and 138.1 ohm-m. Following the curve-type notation for consecutive triplets: the first group (74.2, 27.3, 76.3) follows an H pattern ($r1 > r2 < r3$); the second group (27.3, 76.3, 96.3) follows an A pattern ($r1 < r2 < r3$); and the third group (76.3, 96.3, 138.1) also follows an A pattern ($r1 < r2 < r3$). Consequently, the calculated curve type is HAA. The current on-file classification of K-type is inconsistent with these resistivity values and is flagged for correction.

{"curve_type_stated": "HAA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
